decision: Decision cards are read straight from .frame/decisions.jsonl by scripts/decision-cards.js on every use, never through the spec index.
why: The installed app rewrites the spec index with its own older code, and the index watcher sees only .frame/specs/. Reading the file each time keeps every reader on the same current set.

decision: Cards are written only through decision.js add, which assigns the id and date and checks the source and relations; a card is never edited, a newer one supersedes it.
why: An agent writes the card and Frame validates it, so every rule an agent could get wrong is checked rather than trusted. Superseding keeps the history and the union merge line-safe.

decision: No hook delivers a spec card; only spec-less cards reach agents, at edit, prompt, /spec.new and task-run time.
why: A spec already reaches agents through its own history and topic lines. Whether a spec card should replace them is left to the final measurement.

decision: Cards are what gives way under a host's inline cap: one line each before any card is dropped, a dropped card unmarked, each card sent at most once per session.
why: The close reminder and spec history were there first and must arrive whole. A card left out is delivered on a later edit or prompt instead of being lost.

decision: A project without decision.js owes no cards and a project without decisions.jsonl gets byte-identical hints, catalogs, prompts and close checks.
why: That identity is the spec's acceptance bar, and tests pin the no-card hook and spec-context output against the scripts before this spec. The new instruction block is the one intended difference.

decision: The decision rules ship as their own managed block that overrides the add-without-asking line, and their prose names the card file as decisions.jsonl, never by its .frame/ path.
why: The PROJECT_NOTES rules are user-owned and never upgraded. docsHealth reports every named .frame/ path that is missing, and most projects have no card file.

decision: In repo mode .frame/.gitattributes merges decisions.jsonl by union, so cards two branches each add never conflict; local mode writes nothing there.
why: Cards are append-only lines, so keeping both sides is always the right merge. The rule lives inside .frame/ because the project root is the user's.

decision: Decision cards have their own view under Context in the left nav, and the dock Decisions tab keeps listing PROJECT_NOTES.md entries until it retires.
why: The user wanted a view that shows only cards, and chose the nav over a second dock tab. Add, undo and delete come in a later step.
